title: Prompting Claude to diagnose and rewrite slow analytics queries
text: Column. So, what is it about query A's where clause that takes the index away? The function. Query A wraps posted at an STRF time, so the database no longer has a column to look up. It has an expression, and the only way to evaluate it is to visit every row. Query B leaves the column bare and compares it to constants. That is the insight. An index works on the column, not on a function of the column. Let's recap with Claude. One takeaway you can use today. Before you optimize an analytics query, run explain and look for the word scan.
